newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STOCKS INCH HIGHER ON UPBEAT CONSTRUCTION.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STOCKS INCH HIGHER ON UPBEAT CONSTRUCTION.

text.p: Greek shares extended their recent gains with a 0.24 percent rise in early Thursday trades.
Construction continued to lead the market higher on the back of Wednesday's 2.15 percent advance in their sector sub-index.
They were up 0.90 percent 30 minutes into the session.

"Construction stocks seem to consolidate ahead of the announcement on the host city for the 2004 Olympic Games and I expect prices to play up very shortly," said Costas Panagidis, general manager at Axon Securities.
An announcement for the host city for the Games is expected on September 5. Athens along with Rome are the favourites, with Stockholm, Cape Town and Buenos Aires trailing behind in the odds.

"Looking beyond the construction sector, hosting the games will necessitate a great deal of additional telecoms, transportation and other infrastructure projects, boosting the entire economy over a prolonged period, even after the Games are behind us," he added.
The Athens bourse will be closed on Friday August 15 in observation of the Assumption of the Virgin. The next trading session will be staged on Monday August 18.
Salomon Brothers downgraded Greek stocks to underweight short term and neutral long term in its August emerging Europe strategy report from neutral short and long term a month earlier.
It said Greek equities had become expensive with a market price earnings ratio (P/E) of 12 and expected further correction for the rest of the year.
"Market participants do keep an eye on the views of foreign investors and institutions," Panagidis said.
But sentiment is mostly affected by positive reports and local investors are reluctant to endorse bearish views.

"Even if we accept the theory that the market turned back after the release of Salomon's report, the magnitude of the index's downturn -- around five points -- shows that market sentiment was not seriously dented," he said.
Carnegie, also issued a strategy report on the prospects of the Greek economy and its stock market and anticipated a rise in the bourse's benchmark index to 1,700 in September.

"I believe a key issue to the future course of Greek equities is the level of interest rates which seem to have reached a critical point in view of the large fiscal needs of the government in September," said Panagidis.
"At this stage it looks like interest rates would have to go up if the government opts for tapping the local market rather than resorting to external financing in favourable terms," he added.

Greece's ficsal needs for September are estimated at 2.1 trillion drachmas and local newspapers have carried reports suggesting that the government will seek to raise $2.0 billion to top up its cash reserves.
The Athens benchmark index was up 0.23 percent or 3.76 points to 1,646.12 from Wednesday's 1,642.36 after 30 minutes of trading.
Besides construction, industrials were also up by 0.63 percent with banks trading 0.09 percent lower.
Turnover was 1.5 billion drachmas on volume of 0.3 million shares.
Advancers were leading decliners 76 to 39 with 33 shares unchanged on 148 traded.
